Scene: inside a humble traditional Japanese mountain cottage during a winter afternoon, the old man sits on the wooden floor finishing a woven straw hat in his lap. Exactly FIVE hats total: ONE unfinished conical straw hat held naturally by his two hands, and FOUR completed straw hats neatly arranged beside him so their separate brims can be counted. A modest bundle of loose straw on the floor, simple timber beams and a small wooden lattice window overlooking snow and distant evergreens. He wears a pale cotton head towel tied around his forehead with the little grey topknot visible. Warm soft daylight catches golden straw and his thoughtful face. Three-quarter view with the man left of centre and the completed hats on the right. No other people, no food, no statues. Show real interwoven straw texture without fussy visual clutter. This is the quiet hopeful beginning, not a celebration.
